subject: Stakely renewal — coordinating parachute buffer, billing window, and co-terming
messages:
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: Elena Park <ep@stakely.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Stakely renewal — coordinated option to smooth ramp and temporary 'parachute' buffer

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per your ask, I pulled together a pragmatic renewal structure that tries to hit three priorities you mentioned: (1) simplify the billing window (align to calendar-year co-term), (2) provide a temporary buffer for Q1 ramp risk (we're calling this a "parachute" credit bucket), and (3) preserve an auto-renew option but with a 60‑day opt-out for procurement.

Key proposal (attached as Stakely_Renewal_Draft_v1.pdf):
- Term: 24 months starting 2027-01-01, co-term to calendar year.
- Ramp schedule: Year 1: 40% committed, Year 2: 100% committed (linear monthly ramp).
- Parachute buffer: 250k token-credit buffer available in Q1 of Year 1 to absorb onboarding/early‑usage spikes; unused portion converts to one-time credits applied to the next invoice.
- Billing: Consolidated annual invoice, invoiced at contract start with quarterly true-ups; optional monthly invoice for procurement if they insist.
- Auto-renew: On by default after end of term; procurement has 60 days to opt-out before renewal.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Quick alignment call with procurement and finance to confirm opt-out language and invoicing cadence (Calendly link below).
2) If procurement approves, legal can prepare a short amendment and SOW to capture ramp milestones.
3) We can include a limited overage bucket (metered) for the first 90 days after ramp to avoid surprises.

I've CC'd Marissa to help with pricing details and Neha for billing cadence. I've attached a draft SOW for comments.

If that looks reasonable, can we lock a 30‑minute slot this week? https://calendly.com/lauren-redwood/renewal-sync

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
[Attachment: Stakely_Renewal_Draft_v1.pdf (PDF)]

From: Elena Park <ep@stakely.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T13:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stakely renewal — coordinated option to smooth ramp and temporary 'parachute' buffer

Thanks Lauren — this is really helpful and much closer to what our procurement team will accept. A few notes from procurement and ops:

- Procurement wants the billing window consolidated but would prefer invoices on an annual cadence with an explicit true-up run on month 6 and month 12 (helps with internal forecasting).
- On parachute: procurement is ok with a credit buffer but needs a clear burn report and a cap of $25k/month drawdown — after that we switch to metered overage.
- Auto-renew opt-out: 60 days is acceptable but procurement will ask Legal to validate the language; also asking for a 30‑day early notice for price increases.

I'll loop procurement@stakely.com onto the next call. Can you also confirm whether the parachute credits are refundable if unused or if they convert to pre-paid credits?

We can do a call tomorrow 9:30–10:00 PT — I'll accept the Calendly invite if that slot is open.

— Elena
VP, Customer Ops — Stakely

Elena / procurement team —

Great notes, thank you. Quick answers:
- Parachute credits: Will convert to pre-paid credits on the customer account if unused at the end of Q1; not refundable to cash. We will provide a monthly burn report (token-level summary + dollar impact).
- Billing cadence: We can do annual invoice up front with 6‑ and 12‑month true-ups — I'll flag Neha to confirm accounting treatment.
- Cap: We'll enforce a $25k/month drawdown; any draw beyond that becomes metered overage billed monthly.

Marissa — can you confirm the pricing model with the parachute bucket and the proposed ramp? Also worth deciding if the parachute should be DG (discounted) credits or full-rate credits.

Neha — can you confirm whether annual upfront invoicing with mid-term true-ups requires any special AR workflow or can be done through our standard billing flow?

If everyone is aligned, I'll get Legal (Karthik) the amended term language and SOW for a quick redline.

Thanks,
Lauren

[Attachment: SOW_Stakely_2027.docx (DOCX)]

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, Elena Park <ep@stakely.com>, procurement@stakely.com

Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stakely renewal — coordinated option to smooth ramp and temporary 'parachute' buffer

All — happy to confirm pricing structure. Proposal summary:

- Year 1 committed spend (40% baseline): $300k commitment at 40% of Year 2 projected volume.
- Parachute buffer: $30k credit pool for the first 90 days (capped to $25k/month drawdown as requested).
- Year 2 committed spend: $750k (100% target).
- If usage lags >20% below ramp in Month 3, we will execute a 30‑day review and can convert unused commitment into service credits per the SOW.

Discounting: Parachute credits are treated as pre-paid credits at the same effective rate as the committed units (not an additional discounted SKU) — this keeps accounting straightforward.

I will prepare a short pricing exhibit to insert into the SOW. Karthik, when you get a chance can you draft the amendment language for the co‑terming and auto‑renew opt-out (60 days) and confirm the clause for price increase notices (30 days)?

Lauren — I've added a one‑pager with the tier math; happy to walk procurement through it on the call.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Park <ep@stakely.com>, procurement@stakely.com
Date: 2026-08-24T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Stakely renewal — coordinated option to smooth ramp and temporary 'parachute' buffer

Looping in final legal notes. Draft amendment language (high level):

- Term & Co‑terming: 24‑month term commencing 2027‑01‑01; parties agree to common calendar-year co‑term; amendment to the Master Services Agreement (MSA) to reflect new term.
- Parachute credits: Defined as pre-paid service credits, non-refundable; unused credits roll to account balance as pre-paid units; draw capped at $25,000 per calendar month unless mutually agreed.
- Billing & True-ups: Customer will be invoiced annually in advance; true-up reports at month 6 and month 12; material disputes to be raised within 30 days of true-up.
- Auto‑renew & Price Increase: Contract auto-renews for successive 12‑month periods unless Customer provides written notice of non‑renewal at least 60 days prior to renewal; Provider to provide 30 days notice for any price increases that would take effect on renewal.

I'll prepare formal amendment and send for signature once finance confirms the prefered invoicing object code. Also, include a short SOW exhibit listing ramp milestones (Month by month expected token volumes).

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
